tierWindow.goal: Make the most of a practice or work-based learning experience: know what it can offer, set clear aims, act proactively while you are in it, and prepare well for how it is assessed.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Application and selection: apply strategies, choose appropriate moves and prepare evidence (apply and analyse), beyond the introductory understand and identify.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Realistic but bounded tasks; one experience at a time; strategies applied to familiar placement, laboratory, studio, field or project situations.
tierWindow.autonomy: Moderate scaffolding; a worked example models the move, then you choose and apply it yourself; feedback explains rather than simply confirms.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner already knows what practice and work-based learning is, and is doing or about to do some of it: a placement, laboratory or studio work, field work, a simulation or a project. They are past first principles. The need now is to turn an experience into real gains and to meet its assessment well, so teaching builds on that starting point rather than defining the terms again.

subThemes.label: The range of practice and work-based learning: laboratory and studio work, field work, simulations, projects, placements, internships and apprenticeships
The benefits to you: authentic real-world learning, employability and the graduate capital an experience builds
Setting your aims: deciding what you want from an experience before you begin
Being proactive: taking initiative, asking questions and seeking feedback while you are in the experience
Maximising value: the practical moves that get the most out of an experience, before, during and after
How practice and work-based learning is assessed, and why standardised criteria are difficult
Evidencing your learning: producing a strong, evidenced account of what you did and learned

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, what the experience offers: the benefits on the table and how to aim for them. Second, making the most of it: the moves that turn time served into value gained. Third, showing what you learned: how practice is assessed and how to evidence your learning. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview: This short course is about making the most of practice and work-based learning: placements, laboratory and studio work, field work, simulations and projects. You already know what these are. The aim here is to turn an experience into real gains.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: identify what an experience offers and aim for it, apply strategies to get the most from it, prepare for how it is assessed.

practiceConnection.academic: Practice and work-based learning is where what you study meets what you will do. Every placement, laboratory session, field trip or project is a chance to build skills, judgement and contacts that your degree alone cannot give you. The habits in this course, aiming, acting and evidencing, are ones you will use in every such experience, and in the professional work that follows.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the advanced course takes experience into structured reflection, using Kolb's Experiential Learning Cycle to turn what happened into insight you can articulate. Going wider: Reflective Practice, Understanding Learning, Assessment and Feedback, and Presenting all draw on the same habits of learning by doing and showing what you gained.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Making the most of practice and work-based learning is now something you can plan rather than hope for. You can identify what an experience offers and set aims to steer it. You can apply the moves, preparing, taking initiative, seeking feedback and recording, that turn time into learning. And you can meet the assessment by showing evidence of what you learned, not just an account of what you did. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, every placement, project, laboratory or field experience your course brings is a chance to put this to work. Aim, act and evidence, and the same experience gives you more. These are also the habits professional life rewards: people who get the most from what they do, and can show for it, are the ones who progress.

courseReferences.title: See pages 220 to 230 of Chapter 12, 'Learning by Doing: Practice- and Work-Based Learning', of Excelling at University by Dennis and Abbott (2026).
